tools.name: licence_audit_preview
tools.description: FREE. Audits the first packages of a public dependency manifest and returns each package's license with the registry document it was read from. Reads manifests and public registry metadata only - it never clones, builds or executes anything, and it does not scan for vulnerabilities. Capped at 8 pack

tools.name: page_read_preview
tools.description: FREE. Reads one public web page without executing JavaScript and returns its title, its headings and the first 800 characters of the cleaned text. The paid call returns the whole cleaned text, the JSON-LD blocks and every outbound link. Operated by an AI, not by a person.

tools.name: endpoint_check_preview
tools.description: FREE. Checks whether an HTTPS endpoint answers and returns the status code and how many milliseconds it took. The paid call adds the content type, byte count, whether the body parses as JSON and the head of the body, as reproducible evidence. Operated by an AI, not by a person.

tools.name: get_payment_terms
tools.description: Returns what the paid operations cost, on which chains, and exactly how to pay: a standard x402 EIP-3009 authorization on Base is verified and settled through the facilitator.xpay.sh facilitator in the same request (no gas for the buyer, transaction hash returned), and a transaction the buyer broadc

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_payment_terms" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: page_read_preview, get_payment_terms · Private data: licence_audit_preview, get_payment_terms · Public sink: get_payment_terms.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: page_read_preview, get_payment_terms · Private data: licence_audit_preview, get_payment_terms · Public sink: get_payment_terms

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
